newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank leaves interest rates unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank leaves interest rates unchanged.

text.p: The German central bank left key interest rates unchanged Thursday at the regular meeting of its council.
The Bundesbank also announced it was leaving its targets for 1997 and 1998 M3 money supply growth unchanged, in line with market expectations.

The bank left the discount rate at 2.50 percent and the Lombard emergency financing rate at 4.50 percent. The central bank's main money market rate, the repo, was also held steady at 3.0 percent for the next two weeks.

The M3 target for 1997 was kept at 3.5 percent to 6.5 percent growth in the aggregate compared with its average level in the final quarter of 1996. For 1998, the central bank set an orientation marker for M3 growth of 5 percent.
The Bundesbank said that, despite problems with M3 in recent years, it continued to see M3 money supply as the main marker for its monetary policy.
The central bank targets M3 in the belief that it offers a good indication of future inflationary trends. However, the figure has often been open to sharp distortions.
